output_json.diff_review: Inspected patch_only.diff and confirmed (via `git diff --stat` and `git status --porcelain` in the actual worktree) that the patch touches exactly 3 files: src/main/java/org/owasp/validator/css/CssValidator.java (+134/-1, new methods only), src/main/java/org/owasp/validator/css/CssHandler.java (2 one-line call-site swaps: lexicalValueToString→lexicalValueToOutputString, and selectorName→escapeSelectorForOutput(selectorName)), and src/test/java/.../AntiSamyTest.java (+96, 3 new regression tests + 3 small helper methods). The PoV harness files under .security-pipeline/pov/ are untracked/new (not modified) — confirmed the patch does not touch, weaken, or special-case the PoV in any way. The fix is minimal, targeted, well-commented, and does not alter CSS validation/acceptance logic (only output-serialization safety), which is the correct scope per the alert's regression_hint (fix inside org.owasp.validator.css at CssValidator.lexicalValueToString/CssHandler.property/startSelector, not a downstream serializer patch).
output_json.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` independently via the docker wrapper against the current (patched) worktree. Output: check 1 raw DOM attr is `font-family: a"b;` (no literal '\"'), check 2 raw DOM attr is `font-family: <script>alert(1)</script>;` (no literal '<'/'>'), both checks report `false`, script prints "NOT VULNERABLE ..." and exits 1. This matches the orchestrator's pov_after_patch log exactly and confirms the vulnerability no longer reproduces. The PoV itself was not modified by the patch (verified via git status showing it as untracked, unrelated to the 3 modified product/test files).
output_json.regression_result: Independently reran (docker wrapper, project container): `mvn -B -DskipTests package` → BUILD SUCCESS. `mvn -B test` (full suite, not just AntiSamyTest) → Tests run: 103, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS, across all 8 test classes (AntiSamyTest 69, ESAPIInvalidPolicyTest 8, LiteralTest 4, AntiSamyMalformedPolicyTest 4, PolicyTest 14, AntiSamyPerformanceTest 1, TagMatcherTest 1, TagTest 2). Investigated an apparent discrepancy (AntiSamyTest.java has 72 @Test-looking occurrences in the source but only 69 ran) and confirmed it's a non-issue: 3 pre-existing tests (testGithubIssue24, testGithubIssue34a, testGithubIssue34b) are wrapped in a /* */ block comment (pre-dating this patch, unrelated to it), so the real active test count is 66 pre-existing + 3 new patch-added tests = 69, all passing. No tests were removed or disabled by the patch; git diff confirms only additive changes to the test file.
output_json.summary: The patch fixes the CWE-079 CSS-to-DOM smuggling vulnerability at its root cause in org.owasp.validator.css, exactly matching the alert's regression_hint. It adds CssValidator.lexicalValueToOutputString() (HTML-entity-encodes '\"','\'','<','>','&' in SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI values) and CssValidator.escapeSelectorForOutput() (neutralizes '<' in selector/condition text), and wires both into CssHandler.property()/startSelector() — the single shared code path used by both the inline style-attribute sink (AntiSamyDOMScanner:517) and the <style>-tag sink (AntiSamyDOMScanner:425-431) named in the alert trace. Validation-only logic (lexicalValueToString, isValidProperty, isValidSelector) is untouched, so accepted/rejected CSS is unchanged — only how already-accepted CSS text is serialized into the DOM changed. I independently rebuilt and reran everything in the docker container rather than trusting the logs.
